items.title: Maria Schneider interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: I know Kenny Werner uses things, and he turns things upside down and tries all different combinations of things and he writes beautiful music.

ctx.x: But musically there might not be too much behind it.

Yeah I do all my writing just in front of score paper and then using a piano. I don’t use synthesizers. Some people use it to really develop their ideas. I know Kenny Werner uses things, and he turns things upside down and tries all different combinations of things and he writes beautiful music. And he said he comes up with things he would never come up with if he didn’t have those tools, to try things backwards and, you know, I can believe that. But for me it’s a distraction. Because I need to get, like I was…
Um hum. Speaking of meditation, I think you also said that lately you’ve needed a lot more silence in your life.
